newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China polyester maker mulls listing in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China polyester maker mulls listing in Hong Kong.

text.p: China's Shandong Polyester Co Ltd is planning to issue 270 million H shares, a company official said on Tuesday.
H shares are stock issued by mainland China firms on the Hong Kong bourse.
The timing of the issue is not set and an underwriter has yet to be chosen, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

The firm, based in Jinan, capital of eastern Shandong province, is among the 38 domestic enterprises recently approved by the Securities Commission of the State Council as candidates to offer shares abroad.
The official, who was not named, said the company aims to use the stock proceeds to construct a plant capable of turning out 160,000 tonnes of polyester a year.
The firm also plans to follow the H share offer by applying for an A share issue to tap funds held by domestic investors.
Money raised from the planned second-tranche equity issue would be funnelled into the same project, he added.
The company, which also makes other synthetic fibres, is a subsidiary of the state-owned China Jinan Chemical Fibre Corp, the official said.
